subject: Pilot runway buffer & dev credits request — integration sprint stall
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@novalon.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot blocked by SSO/SAML mismatch — request for runway buffer and dev credits

Hi Olga,

Quick note from the integration team: our SSO vendor is returning intermittent SAML assertions and the connector team hit an unforeseen schema mismatch when we attempted to run the Redwood adapter. That has blocked our QA deploy and the demo window is now at risk.

We are still committed to the pilot but estimations from our engineers suggest another 10–12 business days to resolve and validate. Given that, can Redwood consider a 2-week trial extension and a small sandbox credit top-up so our engineers can continue smoke testing without hitting the quota limits?

Attached are the SAML error logs and a short plan from our CTO (novalon-mvap-plan.pdf). If helpful, Max (cc'd) can share a short recording of the failing flow.

We appreciate the partnership — want to avoid losing momentum in the last mile.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Director of Platform
Novalon

Attachments:
- SAML_error_logs.txt (text)
- novalon-mvap-plan.pdf (pdf)

Folks — forwarding Novalon's note. They hit a SAML/assertion mismatch during adapter integration which has blocked their QA deploy and a demo next week. They asked for a 2-week extension + sandbox credits to avoid quota throttling while engineering digs in.

Ben/Kim: can you confirm credit policy for pilot top-ups (amount, approval path)? Marcus: can you review the attached logs and give an ETA for any Redwood-side mitigations or a recommended temporary configuration (e.g., relaxed timeout or fallback) we can suggest?

Goal: keep the pilot moving and preserve the demo slot; low-cost, time-boxed concession if it prevents churn. If we approve credits, I can reply to Sara with +14 days and the credit amount.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Pilot blocked by SSO/SAML mismatch — request for runway buffer and dev credits

Quick technical read: I reviewed the logs. This is an assertion formatting issue — the adapter is currently failing schema validation when optional attributes are present. It's reproducible in their sample payloads.

Mitigation options (short-term):
- Add a tolerant parser path to skip unexpected attributes (low risk) — ~2 engineer-days to patch + 1 day for QA.
- Provide a temporary config flag to treat certain attributes as optional on the adapter side (very low risk) — ~1 engineer-day and no code change for customers.

Longer term: we should harden the parser and add a regression test in the adapter suite. For this pilot, recommending the temporary config flag + 20k sandbox top-up and 14-day extension from a risk/cost perspective.

If Ben and Olga are good, I can provision the config change and coordinate with Novalon's engineers; that should unblock their QA in 24–48 hours after we flip the flag.

Marcus Lin
Lead Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Hi Sara — thanks for the details and the logs. Good news: we can extend the pilot +14 days and provision a 20k sandbox token top-up to keep your engineers running while you resolve the SAML vendor issue.

What we'll do now:
- Apply a temporary adapter config flag on Redwood's side (Marcus will flip and monitor). Expect unblock within 24–48 hours of the change.
- Add +20,000 sandbox token credit to Novalon's pilot environment.
- Extend the pilot end date by 14 calendar days from the current expiration.

Please note: credits are one-time pilot concessions and will expire if unused after the extension window. We'll record the concession in HubSpot and note the terms in the pilot amendment (I will share the DocuSign link once the amendment is ready).

Kimberly will follow up with a short amendment and the exact expiry language. Marcus will coordinate the config flip and validation with Max. I'll update the HubSpot deal and mark this as a risk-to-close mitigation.

Thanks for partnering — let us know if anything else pops up during validation.

Best,
